frequency_question: How often do major contested federal regulations successfully navigate the notice-and-comment process to final publication within a short administrative window?
membership_rule: Rules categorized as economically significant by OIRA that faced severe initial pushback and legal threats, finalized between 2017 and 2026.

cases.name: EPA Clean Power Plan Repeal / Affordable Clean Energy
EPA Mercury and Air Toxics Standards Reconsideration
Student Loan Forgiveness / Saving on a Valuable Education (SAVE) final rule

provenance_note: rate of 100% from only 6 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 6 named major rules; administrative apparatus almost always succeeds in publishing the final rule if prioritization is high, regardless of friction.
known_gaps: Does not account for rules quietly abandoned before the final rule stage.
skeleton: Contested major rules attempted within a compressed timeframe by determined administrations
multiplier: 6 hits out of 6 documented major test cases achieving final publication within target windows (though subsequent court blocks happen later, the target is specifically reaching final rule publication)
validity_reason: Administrative Procedure Act timelines and OIRA review processes remain stable across the current presidential administration lifecycle.
